findings.title: Group resource name uses group ID, not stable identifier semantics inconsistent with user resource naming
findings.body: resolveGroup returns group.getId() similarly to resolveUser returning user.getId(), but getResourceName() special-cases USERS to map resource.getName() to username while GROUPS has no equivalent branch, so getResourceName for group resources will just return resource.getDisplayName() (likely the raw group id) instead of a human-readable group name. This leaves the UI/representation showing the group id rather than the group name, inconsistent with the Users resource type behavior added in the same change.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission adds resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, resourceStore.findByType is used to iterate resources of type GROUPS, and granted.add(groupResource.getId()) adds the *resource* ID, not the group's model ID. Unlike GroupPermissions (V1) which strips the RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX off the resource name to recover the group ID, V2 resources are created with resource name == group ID (per AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup), so resource.getId() is the authorization resource's internal ID, not the group ID. This will return a set of resource IDs that callers (e.g. UsersResource, session.users().getUsersCount(realm, groupIds)) expect to be actual group IDs, causing user/group filtering based on group membership to silently fail (return no users or wrong set).

findings.title: canList() role check narrowed, removing VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS short-circuit note
findings.body: canList() was changed to `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()`. canView() internally checks MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS roles so behavior is preserved, but the diff removed explicit AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS from the role check in canList and now solely relies on canView() which, in GroupPermissionsV2, performs an authorization policy evaluation hitting the store (hasPermission) even for simple admin-role checks. This introduces extra avoidable policy evaluation overhead on every list check versus the previous hasOneAdminRole short-circuit covering more roles directly.

findings.title: grantIfNoPermission logic changed without accounting for group-based filtering correctly
findings.body: toRepresentation() calls usersEvaluator.grantIfNoPermission(session.getAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) != null) to decide whether canView() should default-grant when there's no explicit permission setup. Previously the group attribute was only set when `!auth.users().canView()`; now it's set whenever groupIds is non-empty regardless of whether the user already has full view permission. This changes grantIfNoPermission's effective semantics subtly (session attribute set even when user canView() is true), which could cause unintended default-grant behavior in edge cases depending on how canView()/grantIfNoPermission interact across requests using the same session.
